card_summary: Fujifilm announced four new broadcast zoom lenses, expanding their product line for live production applications. The announcement was made, with the new lenses designed to work with various camera systems. The new lenses will support 12G-SDI and other interfaces, ensuring compatibility with existing broadcast infrastructure and standards like ST 2110 for real-time transport and AES67 for audio over IP, maintaining signal integrity and frame-accuracy in live production environments.
body_html:
Technical Analysis: Fujifilm's New Broadcast Zoom Lenses Support 12G-SDI and ST 2110 for Reduced Latency

Fujifilm has announced four new broadcast zoom lenses designed to support the latest broadcast standards, including 12G-SDI and ST 2110. These lenses are intended for use in live production environments where low latency and high-quality video are essential. The new lenses will be compatible with a range of broadcast cameras and will support the transport of uncompressed video signals over IP networks using the ST 2110 standard.

Operational ROI

The new Fujifilm broadcast zoom lenses will provide broadcast CTOs with significant operational cost savings by reducing the need for separate signal conversion equipment. By supporting 12G-SDI and ST 2110, these lenses will enable the transport of high-quality video signals over a single cable, reducing the complexity and cost of signal routing. This will result in a lower transmission cost and reduced hardware rack footprint, simplifying the workflow step of signal transport and routing.

In comparison to existing approaches, the use of 12G-SDI and ST 2110 will provide lower latency than traditional satellite or fiber-based transmission methods. This will enable more efficient live production workflows, allowing for faster signal transport and reduced delay between the camera and the production switcher. The reduced latency will also enable more accurate genlock and timing synchronization, resulting in a more stable and reliable signal.

Security & Integration

The new Fujifilm broadcast zoom lenses will integrate seamlessly into existing broadcast IT stacks, supporting the latest standards for signal transport and synchronization, including ST 2110, AES67, and NMOS. The use of these standards will ensure that the lenses are compatible with a range of broadcast equipment and will provide a high level of security and reliability. The lenses will also support the use of JPEG XS compression, enabling the efficient transport of high-quality video signals over IP networks while maintaining a low latency.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: The new Fujifilm broadcast zoom lenses will require a minimum network bandwidth of 10GbE to support the transport of uncompressed video signals over IP networks using the ST 2110 standard. They will also require a compatible broadcast camera and a switcher or router that supports 12G-SDI and ST 2110.
  • Compatibility: The lenses will be compliant with the SMPTE ST 2110-20 standard for the transport of uncompressed video signals over IP networks, as well as the NMOS IS-04 standard for device discovery and registration.
  • What to Watch: Engineers should track the development of new standards and updates to existing ones, such as the upcoming release of the SMPTE ST 2110-22 standard for the transport of compressed video signals over IP networks, which may impact the design and deployment of future broadcast systems.

The introduction of these new broadcast zoom lenses from Fujifilm signals a significant shift towards the adoption of IP-based broadcast systems, with a focus on low latency and high-quality video transport. Engineering teams should begin planning for the deployment of these lenses and the supporting infrastructure, including 12G-SDI and ST 2110-compatible equipment, to take advantage of the operational cost savings and improved signal quality they offer.

Analysis: Fujifilm's new broadcast zoom lenses support 4K resolution, aligning with ST 2110 standards for IP-based broadcast workflows, enabling efficient video transport over IP networks.
